record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.context_brief: Ring of invariants of binary octavics
record.original_question: Determine the invariant theory of binary octavics: compute the ring of invariants of homogeneous degree-8 binary forms over C, including correct generators and algebraic relations.

evidence.quote: Denote by S(n, r) the graded ring of invariants of homogeneous polynomials of order r in n variables over C.
Problem 15. Determine the ring of invariants of binary octavics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V_8 = \mathrm{Sym}^8(\mathbb{C}^2)$ denote the space of binary forms of degree $8$ in variables $x,y$ over $\mathbb{C}$, on which the group $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ acts in the standard way. Let $S(2,8) = \mathbb{C}[V_8]^{\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})}$ be the corresponding graded ring of polynomial invariants of binary octavics.

Determine the invariant theory of binary octavics completely: namely, give an explicit minimal set of homogeneous generators of $S(2,8)$ together with their degrees, and determine a complete set of generators for the ideal of algebraic (syzygy) relations among them, so that $S(2,8)$ is described as a quotient of a polynomial ring by an explicit ideal.
artifact.category_tag: Classical invariant theory of binary forms
artifact.status_search_result: A minimal generating set is classically known: nine invariants of degrees 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10, found by von Gall (1880) and confirmed by Shioda (1967), with the ideal of relations generated in degrees 16–20. However, Shioda's explicit syzygies were later found to contain errors. Subsequent work (e.g., Lercier–Ritzenthaler and follow-ups on hyperelliptic genus-3 moduli) has redefined the invariants and corrected/computed the algebraic relations among them, so the problem is essentially resolved in the literature, though the original formulation of "fully correct generators and relations" was open at the time of posing and has been progressively settled.

status_evidence.title: Invariant of a binary form - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The ring of invariants of a degree 8 form is generated by 9 invariants of degrees 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10. Shioda (1967) confirmed the generators and showed the ideal of relations is generated by elements of degrees 16,17,18,19,20.
status_evidence.claim: Generators and degree of relations are classically known.

status_evidence.title: Some remarks on the hyperelliptic moduli of genus 3
status_evidence.snippet: The syzygies among the SL2(k)-invariants described in Shioda's paper seem to be incorrect; the invariants are redefined and the algebraic relations among them determined.
status_evidence.claim: Shioda's syzygies contained errors that have since been corrected.

status_evidence.title: Hyperelliptic curves and their invariants
status_evidence.snippet: Lercier–Ritzenthaler study invariants of binary forms including degree 8, providing computational treatment.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent computational work has refined the invariant theory of binary octavics.
